ABOUT DOIT

We are focused on reinventing how people spend, save, invest, exchange, travel, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and and become an expert at ease. We believe AI will help make finance smart, assessible and safe.

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. The Role

We are looking for full stack engineers to build fast across Doit's AI Neobank app.

This role is for product-minded engineers who can move across frontend, backend, internal tools and customer journeys to turn ideas into working products quickly.

 


WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - Build and ship full product features across frontend, backend, APIs and databases.

 - Create customer and internal workflows for onboarding, accounts, payments, rewards, travel, FX, support automation, KYC and risk.

 - Turn ambiguous product problems into working systems with clean UX and reliable backend logic.

 - Work closely with product, design, mobile, backend and AI engineers to launch fast and improve after release.

OpenArt is building the platform of visual storytelling with generative AI, empowering creators to tell stories, design worlds, and express ideas with ease and style. We’re looking for a Forward Deployed Creative (FDC) who can help creative teams unlock the full potential of OpenArt.

You’ll work directly with our enterprise clients—including brands, agencies, studios, marketing teams, and other creative organizations—to onboard and educate their teams, demonstrate creative workflows, answer questions, and help them integrate generative AI into the way they create.

The ideal person combines creative craft and taste with deep generative AI knowledge, allowing you to understand what a client is trying to achieve, demonstrate the right workflows, and help their team produce work that meets a professional creative bar.

Your first priority will be enterprise training and education, but you’ll also have opportunities to contribute creatively to OpenArt Studios, working on client projects, creative ideation, workflow development, demos, and experimentation with new models and techniques.

If you love creating with generative AI, teaching others, presenting your ideas, and solving creative problems, this role puts you directly at the intersection of our product, our customers, and the future of AI-powered creativity.

 - Lead onboarding and training for OpenArt's enterprise clients.

 - Teach generative AI through real creative workflows.

 - Become a trusted creative resource for clients.
   
   Answer questions during onboarding and provide occasional follow-up guidance as teams begin incorporating OpenArt into their day-to-day creative process.

 - Adapt training to different creative teams and use cases.

 - Standardize and improve our enterprise training process.
   
   Help turn what we learn from each onboarding into repeatable training frameworks, documentation, demos, best practices, and educational resources that allow us to deliver a consistently excellent experience as we scale.

 - Stay at the forefront of generative AI.
   
   Keep up with the latest image and video models, techniques, workflows, and creative capabilities across the generative AI ecosystem. Experiment with new approaches and understand where different models excel.

 - Contribute creatively to OpenArt Studios.
   
   When not focused on enterprise training, collaborate with the Studios team on client projects, creative ideation, AI production, demos, prompt and workflow development, and experimentation with new creative techniques.

 - Bring client learnings back to OpenArt.
   
   Identify recurring questions, workflow challenges, and creative opportunities you encounter while working with customers and share those insights with the broader OpenArt team.

 - Represent OpenArt confidently.
   
   Present OpenArt in virtual and in-person training sessions, workshops, demos, and other client-facing environments. Be comfortable presenting to groups and explaining creative concepts clearly.

 - Travel when required.
   
   Be willing to travel for client onboarding, workshops, events, or other OpenArt initiatives when needed.


🔎 WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR


CORE REQUIREMENTS

 - A professional creative background is essential. You should come from a creative industry such as film, television, advertising, marketing, design, creative production, or a related field. We’re looking for someone who understands creative craft, has a strong bar for visual quality and taste, and can speak the same creative language as the clients and teams they’ll be working with.

 - Deep hands-on knowledge of generative AI image and video tools, including the latest models, their strengths, limitations, and appropriate creative use cases.

 - A portfolio or body of work demonstrating strong AI-generated image, video, storytelling, commercial, or creative content.

 - Ability to incorporate generative AI into a broader professional creative workflow, rather than simply experimenting with individual prompts.

 - Ability to understand a creative objective and determine the appropriate models, tools, prompts, references, and workflows needed to achieve it.

 - Strong presentation and communication skills, with the confidence to teach and speak in front of groups, both virtually and in person.

 - Ability to explain complex AI concepts and workflows in a way that is clear, practical, and approachable.

 - Comfortable answering questions and troubleshooting creative challenges in real time.

 - Fluent English speaker.

 - Willingness to travel when required.


WHAT MAKES YOU STAND OUT

 - You’ve worked closely with brands, agencies, studios, or enterprise creative teams and understand how their creative processes actually work.

 - You’ve helped build or improve training programs, onboarding systems, playbooks, or educational resources that can scale beyond a single session.

 - You’re comfortable navigating open-ended creative challenges where there may not be an established workflow or obvious solution.

 - You naturally look for ways to turn what you learn into repeatable processes, making the next project, training, or onboarding better than the last.

 - Familiarity with OpenArt is a significant plus, particularly if you already use the platform as part of your creative workflow.

 - Senior-level expertise is a plus, but we're equally interested in exceptional creators and educators who demonstrate strong creative judgment, initiative, and versatility.


SOFT SKILLS

 - Educator mindset: You genuinely enjoy helping other people understand new tools and become better creators.

 - Creative problem solver: You don't just know which buttons to press—you can figure out how to get from a creative idea to the desired result.

 - Strong communicator: You're comfortable explaining, demonstrating, answering questions, and adapting your communication to different audiences.

 - High creative taste: You understand what makes an image, video, or story compelling and can help others improve their work.

 - Curious and experimental: You're constantly exploring new models, workflows, techniques, and possibilities within generative AI.

 - Adaptable: You can work with a sophisticated creative studio one day and a team completely new to generative AI the next.

 - Resourceful and proactive: You're comfortable figuring things out, improving processes, and creating resources when they don't already exist.

 - Collaborative: You can work across clients, Studios, product, marketing, and other teams within OpenArt.


💖 WHY OPENART?

This is an opportunity to help define how some of the world's creative teams adopt and use generative AI.

You won't just be demonstrating software. You'll help brands, agencies, studios, and creative teams rethink what's possible in their creative process—and teach them how to turn those possibilities into real work with OpenArt.

You'll also remain an active creator yourself, collaborating with OpenArt Studios, experimenting with the newest generative AI models, developing new workflows, and helping us continuously improve how we teach and enable creativity at scale.

The things you learn from our customers will help shape how we train the next customer, how Studios creates, and ultimately how OpenArt evolves.


🌍 WORK SETUP

 - We’re a remote-friendly team.

 - Candidates based in the United States are preferred, particularly for easier collaboration and travel with enterprise clients.

 - Hybrid options are available if you're based near the Bay Area.

 - This role may require travel for client training, workshops, events, and other OpenArt initiatives.

 - Visa sponsorship is available.
   
   

We’d love to see:

 - Examples of your strongest AI-generated image, video, storytelling, commercial, or creative projects.

 - Examples that demonstrate your professional creative background and visual taste.

 - Any tutorials, workshops, presentations, educational content, or on-camera work you've created.

**About Tessera Labs**
 Tessera Labs is a new category of enterprise software: an AI platform that changes how the world's largest companies run.
   

  

 Every large enterprise carries the same weight — decades of accumulated process, data, and code that no longer match the business it has become. Changing any of it is a program measured in years and hundreds of millions of dollars, staffed by armies of consultants, and it fails more often than anyone admits. Most companies have quietly accepted this as the cost of being large.
   

  

 We don't. Tessera is a transformation engine: a governed, multi\-agent platform that understands an enterprise's process, data, and code as one connected system and changes it in weeks rather than years. We're vendor\-agnostic by design — SAP, Salesforce, Workday, Oracle, Snowflake, MuleSoft — and tied to none of them.
   

  

 Two things make this hard, and they're the reason the job is interesting. Governance: every action is logged, traceable, and reversible, because our customers are regulated and these are the systems that close their books. And generality: the platform has to work on landscapes it has never seen, at companies whose complexity is genuinely unique to them.
   

  

**We sell a product, not a service.** 
 Our people are here to make the product successful, not the other way around. If you've watched enterprise AI companies quietly become consultancies, that distinction is the one to press us on.
   

  

 We raised a $60M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz, with Foundation Capital, Myriad Venture Partners, and Osage University Partners participating.
   

  

**About The Role**
 Turning platform capability into outcomes a Fortune 500 will bet on has two halves — the systems that surround the model, and the model itself. This role owns the first.
   

  

 You will own agents end to end: the harness they run in, the tools they call, the context they see, the guardrails around them, and the evals that tell us whether any of it is improving. Most of the difficulty is not model access. It's an agent reasoning across a landscape with nineteen years of undocumented decisions embedded in it, where one call silently returns a stale schema forty steps into a plan — and the work of making that failure legible, reproducible, and then impossible.
   

  

 This is not a prototyping role. Everything you build gets pointed at systems a company's quarter close depends on.
   

  

*If the model itself interests you more than the systems around it, look at Research Engineer — same team, other half of the problem.*
**What You'll Do**
* Design and ship the production agents that do transformation work: understanding a landscape, planning a change, executing it across process, data, and code, and proving it was correct.
* Build the tool layer — typed, permissioned, well\-documented interfaces that let agents read and act across enterprise systems without ever exceeding what a human approver authorized.
* Improve agent performance through prompting, context construction, tool\-use strategy, and decision logic — and know which of those a given failure calls for.
* Build the retrieval layer over enterprise artifacts and metadata: chunking and indexing strategies for content that doesn't resemble prose, hybrid search, reranking, grounding, and the evaluation that tells you whether any of it helped.
* Manage context deliberately. Enterprise artifacts are enormous and a forty\-step run accumulates history fast; deciding what the model sees, what gets compressed, and what gets dropped is a first\-class engineering problem here, not a prompt detail.
* Use classical ML where it's the right tool. Plenty of the work inside an agent pipeline — routing, ranking, classification, anomaly detection, confidence estimation — is better served by a small supervised model than by another LLM call, and knowing the difference is part of the job.
* Build the eval and monitoring layer: task sets drawn from real customer landscapes, regression coverage on every deploy, and alerting that catches a changed schema, a revoked authorization, or a new model version before the customer does.
* Instrument every run so each model call, tool invocation, decision, and human approval can be reconstructed afterward. This is what "passes audit" means in practice, and it's a product requirement rather than a nice\-to\-have.
* Diagnose production failures from execution traces down to root cause, then close the gap in the system rather than in a single prompt.
* Design the guardrails, approval gates, and rollback paths that make an agent safe to point at a live enterprise landscape.
* Build capability that generalizes. Anything that only works for one customer is a bug in the product, not a feature of the engagement.


**Representative projects**
* Shipping the agent that lets a customer retire a third of their custom estate in a quarter — and the review surface that makes a human comfortable approving each call in minutes rather than days.
* Designing the approval and write semantics for agents operating in a live landscape, so nothing reaches production without a traceable human decision and no partial failure leaves systems inconsistent.
* Building the reconciliation agent that makes two merged companies' data agree, plus the eval set that tells us when it's confident and when it's guessing.
* Standing up the replay\-evaluation pipeline that scores a candidate agent version against a month of recorded runs — real system responses, mocked writes — so a regression is caught before anything is touched in a customer environment.
* Taking a pattern that worked at one customer and turning it into a platform primitive that works at the next four without a human rewriting it.


**You may be a good fit if you**
* Have 3\+ years building and operating production software, with meaningful recent time on LLM\-powered systems.
* Have shipped agentic systems that real users depend on, and have owned the incident when they broke.
* Are fluent in the current agent toolkit — tool calling, orchestration, context engineering, RAG, evals, tracing — and can say where each one stops working.
* Have built retrieval systems against messy real\-world corpora, and have measured them rather than assumed them.
* Have real traditional ML in your background — supervised learning, feature engineering, model evaluation — and reach for it when it beats a prompt.
* Treat evaluation as engineering rather than a report you generate at the end.
* Think in systems and customer outcomes, not model metrics.
* Are comfortable with non\-determinism and have opinions about building reliably on top of it.
* Write strong Python and are comfortable in TypeScript.
* Ship fast, and verify before you claim it works.
* Find large, ugly, undocumented enterprise systems interesting rather than beneath you. That instinct is most of the job, and it's rarer than it should be.


**Strong candidates may also have**
* Hands\-on experience with enterprise platforms, their APIs, and their extension models — SAP, Salesforce, Workday, Oracle, Snowflake, MuleSoft, ServiceNow.
* Experience with knowledge graphs, ontologies, or semantic models over messy real\-world systems.
* Experience with code analysis, program transformation, or automated refactoring at scale.
* Experience with MCP, sub\-agents, or agent skill/plugin architectures.
* A background in distributed systems or workflow engines, where partial failure is the default case.
* Experience at an early\-stage startup or as a founder, where scope was whatever needed doing that week.
* Familiarity with enterprise security and compliance realities: SSO, RBAC, segregation of duties, PII handling, SOC 2, data residency.


**Join the Future of AI at Tessera Labs**
 We're looking for someone who enjoys building reliable, scalable systems that help teams move faster. If you take pride in cutting\-edge AI, value clear ownership, and want to have a meaningful impact in a fast\-moving environment, you’ll fit right in.

Join the team as Twilio’s next Machine Learning Engineer, Customer Memory.
About the job
This position is needed to build and scale the pipelines that turn raw conversation data into structured, searchable customer memory, and the evaluation systems that keep that memory accurate as the product evolves.
You'll join the Conversation Memory team, which builds the memory layer behind Twilio's Conversational AI platform: the systems that extract what matters from millions of conversations, resolve it to the right customer, and retrieve it in milliseconds when an agent needs it. Memory that is wrong, stale, or crossed between customers is worse than no memory at all, so quality measurement is a first-class part of the work.
Responsibilities
In this role, you’ll:
Build the extraction pipeline that turns raw data into structured memory, tuning the LLM prompts and schemas that decide what an AI agent remembers about a customer and what it forgets.
Own the retrieval path that answers "what do we know about this person?" in milliseconds, working with embeddings, vector search, and ranking
Contribute to the eval systems that tell us whether memory is actually getting better, turning a fuzzy question of quality into benchmarks and regression gates that run before every change ships.
Diagnose production issues across the ingestion, extraction, and indexing path using logs, metrics, and traces.
Partner with Product and ML teams to translate customer problems into system changes and evaluation criteria.
Qualifications
Twilio values diverse experiences from all kinds of industries, and we encourage everyone who meets the required qualifications to apply. Experience building backend services, and a demonstrated ability to pick up new languages, frameworks, and tools as the problem demands.
A curious approach to service management: ability to investigate how systems actually behave in production, and desire to continuously learn how to operate them with rigor and accountability.
Experience building or working with evaluation/quality-measurement systems, such as regression detection or quality metrics, or the desire to learn.
Solid grounding in observability practices: structured logging, metrics, and using them to debug distributed systems in production.
Fluency with AI-assisted dev tools (e.g. agents for code generation, review, debugging), applied with deliberate direction and critical thinking.

Experience with Go and/or Python.
Experience with event-streaming systems (e.g. Kafka).
Experience building LLM-backed products.
Practical experience applying ML, e.g. building, evaluating, or productionizing models.

Stay alert to recruitment fraud
We care about your safety. Scammers sometimes impersonate Twilio recruiters through fake job postings, emails, websites, or messages. Please ensure you are engaging with an official @ twilio.com email address. We will never ask for payment, gift cards, cryptocurrency, or banking information during the recruiting process. We do not make job offers without a formal interview process or conduct interviews exclusively through text-based messaging apps.
